cards.label: {today} — Whitechapel
cards.text: Rent's due Monday. £350. You have £40, and this morning's interview did not go well. Archie, an old mate, said he might have work. So: Tuesday night, behind a chicken shop on Mile End Road.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: He's whistling, a Tesco bag hooked on one finger. "Awright, Sherlock?"
You pull a face; you stopped liking that nickname when your age hit double digits.
"Two blokes, cash, in and out before the chicken shop shuts. Nothing to worry about, it's just like a sale off Craigslist."
cards.speaker: Archie

cards.text: "Need me to do anything?"
cards.speaker: You

cards.text: "You just stand there and use your eagle eye to spot anything troublesome."
cards.speaker: Archie

cards.text: During events, you can tap here to use items, or observe. Observing can give you insights into what's happening around you, which may give you advantages.
Try it now. Tap here, then tap 'observe'.
"So then, Holmes, anything we should worry about?"
cards.speaker: Archie

pick.reason: You didn't spot anything worth mentioning.

physics.result_text: "One way in, one way out. Past the boxes." Archie gives you a long look. "Then keep your eyes open."
"Ground's wet. Bad for running." "Bad for everyone, Sherlock." Archie shrugs it off.

life.result_text: "Nobody about. Nobody to see anything, either." Archie gives you a long look. "Keep your eyes open, then."
"Dead quiet round here." "Handy, that." Archie doesn't look up.

emotion.result_text: "You're whistling. What aren't you telling me?" Archie gives you a long look. "Just keep your eyes open."
"You're whistling." "Good mood, that's all." Archie keeps whistling.

time.result_text: "Funny time for a straight deal, this." Archie gives you a long look. "Keep your eyes open."
"They're late." "It's the A13. They're always late." Archie checks his phone.

fate.result_text: "Got a bad feeling about this, Arch." Archie gives you a long look. "Keep your eyes open."
"Bad day, all in all." "Cheer up, Sherlock. It can only get better." Archie grins.

cards.text: "I'm sure it's fine. Anyway, just stand there looking like intimidating. If I say leg it, you leg it. Don't wait for me."
cards.speaker: Archie
You
cards.text: "I don't look like I'd be a pain to fight."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Pretend you're Vinnie Jones in his prime, then." He looks you up and down. "Bit more of a Mr Bean vibe, but you make do with what you've got." He holds out a fist. "You in?"

choices.label: "I'll stand there."
choices.result_text: You bump the fist. "Lovely," says Archie, and goes back to whistling.

choices.label: "Who are the buyers?"
choices.result_text: Archie lowers the fist. "Two lads from Romford. Bought off me twice. Pay cash, don't chat." He thinks about it. "One of them's got a cousin. Never met the cousin."

choices.label: "I want half."
choices.result_text: "You were getting half." Archie looks at you for a long second, fist still out. "Sixty-forty, then. Your way. Don't make a habit of it."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: He pulls something from his pocket and presses it into your hand: a small glass hourglass, warm. "Keep this to hand. If it goes bad, break it." He doesn't say what it does. He's already watching the road.

choices.label: Take it
choices.result_text: You put it in your pocket, where it keeps being warm.

cards.text: The buyers arrive in a grey Vauxhall. Three of them, one more than Archie mentioned. He stops whistling.

cards.label: It goes wrong
cards.text: The third man gets out last, in no hurry. The other two straighten up. They call him Nick. He holds out a hand for the Tesco bag, looks in, and hands it back. "Light." Nobody has said a number. One of the others opens a Stanley knife.

cards.speaker: Nick
cards.text: He looks you over and takes his time about it. "New one. Lovely. Stay there, newbie. You can watch." He's smiling before the sentence is finished.
Nick cracks his knuckles, one at a time. Archie edges half a step in front of you.

intro: Nick doesn't wait for anyone to be ready.

lessons.1: Archie's down. Nick's coming for you.
lessons.2: Read what he's about to do.
lessons.3: You can't win this. Look at the bar.

cards.text: Your eyes dart left and right, confused. Adrenaline and fear pump through your body. Your attackers are in a bubble, slowed like a video buffering. Nick is still mid-sneer.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Archie walks calmly but briskly around them. "Coming, or what?"

cards.label: Four streets later
cards.text: A closed launderette. Archie leans on the shutter, eyes streaming, the Tesco bag still hooked on his finger. "Pub," he says.

tiers.text: One way into the alley. The chicken shop's back door is stacked with boxes. If this goes wrong, you're going out past the buyers.
The rain has made the ground slippery; not good for getaways, or for tussles.

physics.miss: You accidentally look directly into the light over the chicken shop door. Smooth. Now there's a purple blob wherever you look.

tiers.text: No customers, the chicken shop worker is asleep. No passers-by or cars driving past. Whatever happens back here, no one will see it.
The night is still. Not a lot of movement around here, though to be fair it is late.

life.miss: Across the street, a pigeon's working on a chip bigger than its head. You watch it longer than you should.

tiers.text: Archie's always calm under pressure, but you can see there's something bothering him. He seems glad you're here.
Archie's whistling; he does that when he's keeping something to himself.

emotion.miss: Archie has a look on his face. Nervous? Excited? Constipated? You're not sure.

tiers.text: Midweek, too late for commuter crowds and too early for anyone out on the town. This is a strange time for a kosher deal.
You and Archie are bang on time, but the buyers still aren't here. Probably stuck in traffic.

time.miss: You can almost hear the footie match on the chicken shop telly. Wonder if this'll be over in time to catch the second half.

tiers.text: You count the people this needs; Archie, you, 2 buyers. Your gut keeps counting one more.
Today has felt like one of those days where everything goes wrong. For some reason that feeling hits you hard right now.

fate.miss: Something smells fishy. Probably the shop. Though they don't do fish.

tiers.text: Hands in their pockets. Light on their feet. Eyes flicking between your eyes and hands, and Archie's. They're expecting something to go wrong.
The way they're looking between you and Archie seems a bit intense.

physics.miss: One of them has really nice shoes. Would it be awkward to ask where he got them?

tiers.text: Their eyes and expressions are keyed up and focused. They're expecting trouble, or looking for it.
The energy changes as they arrive; tense. You feel some adrenaline already entering your system.

emotion.miss: These guys seem nice. Maybe you can get a pint together after this?

tiers.text: Your gut is screaming at you to run, but they're blocking the only exit.
Mum always said life was like a box of chocolates. This seems more like a box of liquorice. You don't like liquorice.

fate.miss: This is probably fine. Right? Right??
